---
title: "Architecture and Data Flow"
---

SCGSim keeps semantic geometry, solver preparation, execution, result loading,
and presentation distinguishable. A solver backend may implement its own
physics, but it must not redefine geometry identity, run identity, or common
provenance.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  G["SGB semantic geometry and topology"] --> B["Solver-specific backend preparation"]
  B --> C["Common run-and-handoff contract"]
  C --> P["Selected machine profile"]
  P --> A["Immutable artifacts and receipts"]
  A --> R["Solver-specific physical results"]
  R --> U["Unified Plotly report envelope"]
```

## Contract boundaries

| Boundary | Authority |
|---|---|
| Geometry names, topology, Route A/B surfaces | SGB |
| Palace and AEDT implementation | Planned `scgsim.palace` and `scgsim.aedt` owners |
| Run identity, handoff, profiles, receipts | One common SCGSim contract |
| Physical result meaning | Solver-specific, never flattened into a false common quantity |
| Report navigation, provenance, cost presentation | Planned unified report envelope |

## Phase-1 truth

At this docs-first base, the architecture is a contract, not an implemented
pipeline. The product candidate is limited to package and version scaffolding;
the backend boxes above are planned.

See [Folder tree and ownership](ownership.qmd) for repository placement.
